title: Rubber Rooms
html:
The main entrance of the Rubber Rooms interior.

The Rubber Rooms are a psych ward themed interior. It most commonly spawns on Xenphir and has a rare chance to spawn on any moon.

> Rooms

  • Reception - The main entrance always generates with a receptionist desk in front of it.
  • Coffin - A coffin in a room typically found near the main entrance. This coffin has the reward for completing a Secondary Objective.
  • Cells - Various small rooms with an assortment of furniture and other items in them.
  • Padded Cells - More confined cells that can connect to the titular Rubber Rooms.
  • Rubber Rooms - Accessed by walking through the fog in some Padded Cells, teleporting players to an area directly above the interior with padded white walls. Scrap can spawn here and entities can enter and leave this area.
  • Morgues - Rooms with several trays for bodies. Players can interact with some of the doors to open a tray and potentially reveal scrap. One of the morgues will only generate trays for the Discover the Body objective.
  • Offices - Larger rooms with large tables, many chairs, etc. Scrap can spawn in them.
  • Library - A section of the interior with several bookshelves. Scrap can spawn here.
  • Cafeteria - A large cafeteria room with a kitchen.
  • Operating Room - A room down a narrow staircase often with the corpse of an employee. Frequently has scrap inside it.
  • Nursery - A room for children with small cradles. A baby is often heard crying until players approach the cradle the sound is coming from. Scrap can spawn here.
  • Haunted Apparatus - A door will open by itself to a long hallway that leads to a room with a door, an electric chair, and a white apparatus. It is worth ▮90, is two-handed, and weighs 8lbs. Taking the apparatus will cause the door to briefly shut and cause blood to come out of the chair. The door will then open back up to a now shifting hallway with the blood surging down it. Players must run back through this hallway without the blood catching up to them or they will die, which is possible if the player weighs 8lbs and begins sprinting the moment the door opens. The door at the end will swing open on its own again before shutting behind the player.

> Interior Features

  • Spooks - Various spooks and scares can occur in the interior, such as an eyeball appearing through the window of a door, lights exploding, book cases falling, etc. These spooks can be disabled in the Magic Wesley Rubber Rooms config.
  • Rats - Sometimes rats can be found skittering around. There are small holes in the wall that they can crawl out of. These are harmless. Rarely, a much larger rat with glowing red eyes can run through the walls with a loud sound effect accompanying it. This is also harmless.
  • Shifting Hallway - A hallway that moves up or down a level after being walked through. This always generates next to the main entrance room. Can be disorienting when trying to navigate.
  • Infinite Hallway - A hallway where the end is shrouded in a dark fog, and passing through the fog transports the player to a hallway that loops so long as they keep walking ahead. Turning around and going back is a good way to get out. The hallway has two different exit points.
  • Eclipsed - When this interior is on a moon that is Eclipsed, bloodstains will be everywhere. Additionally, the Haunted Apparatus hallway will shift more and slightly reduce visibility with a grainy-like effect when pulled.

> Hazards

  • Spooky Door - A red door with an X on it can sometimes be immediately opened and will remain open for the rest of the day. However, if a player opens this door from a specific direction an infinite, mirror-like hallway will apear with a floating head rapidly approaching the player. It will deal 666 damage to the player if not closed in time. The door will take half a second to close with the prompt being replaced with the text "SHUT THE DOOR" and will open itself back up after successfully shutting it. This door can be disabled in the Magic Wesley Rubber Rooms config.
  • Fake Fire Exit - A fire exit door that always spawns on a tile with a black and white floor and red walls. Additionally, the hand symbol that appears for interacting with this door is noticeably bigger than an ordinary door. If a player interacts with it, they will be transported to a hallway where the fire exit is moving away from them and the walls are shrinking. Players reach and exit the fire exit at the end before being crushed. After escaping, the door cannot be interacted with anymore.

> Secondary Objectives

The Coffin that holds the reward.

One of three unique objectives will randomly generate for players to complete for one of three valuable rewards that will spawn after opening the Coffin with a key.

Gut the Corpse

The seat next to the Coffin will spawn a Gutting knife. Players must find the in-tact corpse of an employee nailed to wood in the interior and insert the knife into their stomach. Players must then repeatedly interact with the knife to open up the employees guts.

While the employee's guts fall out, a key will fall to the ground and a sound effect will play. Players can now return to and open the Coffin for their reward.

Discover the Body

A cause of death will be written next to the Coffin. Players must remember this and make their way to one of the Morgues that has eight different trays to open. On the back wall will be an autopsy report for each person and players must open the tray of the named individual that best matches the cause of death description. If a player opens an incorrect tray, a black hand will reach out and crush its fist, dealing 666 damage to all nearby players including players in portions of adjacent rooms.

If players open the correct tray, a key will slide out instead and a sound effect will play. Players can now return to and open the Coffin for their reward.

Pay in Blood

Around the corner in the same room as the Coffin will be a device to place five fingers. Players must find three chairs in Padded Cells and sit in them. They can then repeatedly interact with the cranks on either side to drop a blade onto and slice off their own fingers, dealing 10 damage to themselves. Although players only need five fingers, they can only get out of a chair after slicing off both fingers.

Players can then return to and place each finger on the device. They will be prompted to interact with the screen above the device which will spawn the key to open the Coffin for their reward.

The reward is randomized, but the chance for a more valuable reward is increased by how early in the day players complete the objective and is influenced by the vanilla luck system. The value of the reward is additionally increased by a difficulty multiplier, ranging from 0.6x to 1.4x, and a solo (singleplayer) multiplier of 1.17x. Gut the Corpse is considered Easy difficulty and has a 1.0x multiplier, Discover the Body is considered Medium difficulty and has a 1.15x multiplier, and Pay in Blood is considered Hard difficulty and has a 1.4x multiplier. The base value and multipliers for objective rewards can be adjusted in the Wesleys Interior Tools config under the Secondary Objectives section.

Hailey Robertson

Upon collecting any reward, Hailey Robertson, the woman in the Coffin, will begin haunting players. Spooky sound effects will randomly play followed by a message next to the player's stamina bar, which is Hailey Robertson speaking to them. This haunting persists across all moons barring moons like Galetry and Gordion.

Eventually, Hailey Robertson will announce her prescence with the player's screen turning red and getting a fear effect. This will spawn her as an actual entity, being a variant of the Ghost Girl. She will disappear upon returning to orbit. However, she can spawn once per reward grabbed and continue haunting players if multiple rewards are picked up. This can also apply if players pick up a medallion again after dropping it in the ship, typically after the save file is reloaded.

After Hailey Robertson spawns for the first time on that save file, players will receive a journal entry about her.

HAILEY ROBERTSON

First name: Hailey

Hailey Robertson was found deceased in the treatment room of the Crosswind Mental Hospital, She had signs of physical abuse, lacerations to the back and chest, and a small hole was discovered in her forehead.

A notebook was recovered from a burning bin containing a detailed log of the experiments she was put through. Among which were, being forcefully exposed to violent videos of human torture for days on end without breaks. Being suffocated to the edge of death causing minor brain damage. Having her solve complex logic puzzles within certain timeframes and being punished for failing.

She was often reminded how her four year old son would not be able to survive without her as she was a single mother. This was with the promise of her being let go if she complied.
Unfortunately he also died of starvation during her capture.

A tiny rod was used to destroy a small part of her brain which likely led to her losing any sort of self. This was one of the final experiments listed within the notebook.

Hailey Robertson was one of many victims of such experiments and life altering treatments by the hands of Solover Underhill, the head psychiatrist of the Crosswind Mental Hospital.

She was a loving, hard working mother who had a hard time following her husband’s passing. She was full of courage and remained positive even during her hardest times.
She will be remembered by all.
May she Rest in Peace.

> Event: Void Rooms

An annotated and rough map of the Void Rooms.

The Void Rooms are accessed by walking into a pair of floating white eyes in the interior that disappear when a player gets close to them. If a player walks close enough to the eyes, they will be teleported straight down into a separate part of the interior. Although the Void Rooms almost always spawn, the floating eyes can sometimes spawn in walls and make them practically inaccessible. Multiple players can enter the Void Rooms, but they can not be accessed again after players leave them.

The Void Rooms are a large, dark, and maze-like recreation of the ordinary Rubber Rooms. Shadowy figures are present and watch the player, disappearing when a player gets close to them. Some objects and furniture also disappears upon getting close to them. Currently, the layout of the rooms is always the same but walls connecting or disconnecting some paths is random. Faint white lines on the floor can be used as navigation towards the exit, but can lead to dead-ends. The exit to the Void Rooms always generates in the library at the top left of the map.

When a player enters the Void Rooms, two Void-Heads will immediately spawn. This is a variant of the Coil-Head that does not move while in its patrolling state but behaves similarly otherwise. One Void-Head will spawn in the bottom right corner of the Void Rooms while the other will spawn in front of the exit door.

Void Items

Additionally, the Void Rooms generates 11 Void Items. This scrap currently generates in the same locations, but the scrap itself is randomized. Any Void Items players collect are their reward for the event.

> Trivia

  • The Void Rooms existed prior to the Obscurity update, but had a much simpler and plain layout. They also only spawned one Void-Head and only spawned 1-4 scrap from the moon's scrap table.
  • Prior to the Obscurity update, entities could not enter or leave the Rubber Rooms part of the interior.
  • The monstrous graffiti on the walls is a reference to s1ckboy, a lethal company modder who is also credited with testing and helping with miscellaneous things for Wesley's Moons.
